The process

From the first conversation to a system people use.

Each stage has a clear purpose and a clear result. There are no hidden steps and no confusion about what happens next.

01

Understand the situation

We start with the business problem, not a pre-selected tool.

We discuss your customers, current website, workflows, tools, team and the outcome that matters most.

02

Recommend the right start

We assess your existing systems as part of onboarding, recommend the plan that fits, and say what the first month should deliver.

If we are not the right fit, we will say so early.

03

Define scope and responsibilities

Before work begins, you receive a written proposal covering the outcome, deliverables, timeline, investment, payment terms, client responsibilities, exclusions and third-party costs.

04

Build, connect and test

We design and deliver the agreed website, workflow, automation, integration or training programme.

We share progress at agreed stages and involve you where decisions are needed.

05

Handover and adoption

We test the completed work, provide agreed documentation, transfer relevant ownership and train the people who need to use the system.

06

Improve over time, where valuable

Each month you choose the priorities within your plan’s allowance. We advise on risks and dependencies, deliver and test the work, document it and send a summary of what changed. Unused allowance does not roll over.

Working principles

Five rules that decide how the work runs.

Outcome before tools. We select or improve tools because they support a business outcome, not because a platform is fashionable.

Scope before delivery. We define what is included and excluded before work begins, so expectations stay clear.

Ownership stays with the client. Client domains, accounts, source files and data remain under client ownership wherever possible.

Communication without jargon. We explain work in practical business language and make technical decisions understandable.

Change is managed clearly. Work outside an agreed scope or monthly capacity is quoted and approved before delivery begins.
